title: Request Thread Lane Visualizer Prototype for Async Spans & Rollout Correlation
creator: Marcus Patel
description:
Problem: The current Trace Inspector in Redwood Console surfaces spans in a single timeline but struggles to represent asynchronous execution (callbacks, worker fan-out, queue hops) and to surface which rollout/variant (canary vs stable) influenced a request. This makes root-cause debugging for regressions introduced by rollouts or async code paths slow and error-prone.

Goal: Design a compact, scannable lane-based visualizer that groups spans into logical "threads" (lanes) derived from correlation IDs and inferred async edges. The visualizer should make it easy to: 1) spot cross-thread latencies and gaps, 2) follow an end-to-end request across services and workers, and 3) correlate spans to rollout variants and feature flags directly in the trace view.
design_notes:
High-level approach:
- Lane grouping: Each lane represents a logical execution thread or affinity group (e.g., request handler, background worker, downstream batch job). Lanes are computed from correlation IDs and a lightweight heuristic for async handoffs (queue IDs, spawn/span tags).
- Thread-sequencing: Within lanes, spans are ordered by start time and visually compressed to show density. Async hops create connector edges between lanes.
- Rollout badges: A small badge on the root span and on any span that executed under a different rollout variant (service header/metadata) shows variant id and rollout tag. Hover reveals rollout metadata and links to the Rollouts console page.
- Playback & scrubber: Time scrubber with play/pause to step through request timeline. Scrubber can step by span edges or fixed ms. Playback highlights active lanes and fades out past spans.
- Filters & queries: Filter by correlation-id, rollout variant, latency threshold, span attribute, service name. Quick presets: "Async-fanout", "Queue-wait > 200ms", "rollout=canary".
- Compact & expanded lanes: Compact mode hides small spans and shows only aggregates; expand shows full span list.
- Deep-linking: Permalink includes trace id, focused correlation-id, lane selection, and scrubber position so customers can share exact investigation state.

Design tradeoffs and decisions:
- Lane inference on the client vs server: For performance and consistent sharing, we recommend a server-side pre-processing step to annotate spans with lane_id and edge metadata. Client-side fallback will run a deterministic heuristic when server annotations missing.
- Visual density: To support high token counts in traces, we introduce a level-of-detail compression algorithm (aggregate bar for >n spans).
- Accessibility: Keyboard navigation between lanes and spans, aria labels for badge and connectors, color-safe palette for lane colors.
- Performance budget: Frontend should render a 1k-span trace without blocking UI for more than 150ms on modern machines; we will start with a 250ms soft budget while optimizing.

Open questions for engineering:
- What metadata are we guaranteed on hosted traces that we can use to infer async edges? (e.g., queue IDs, correlation headers)
- Can we add a pre-processing Lambda that annotates lane ids for Dedicated/Private customers as an optional step?
- Backend storage implications for storing lane annotations and connector edges (size delta estimate).
acceptance_criteria: Lane grouping is visible for traces with inferred async edges and can be toggled on/off.
Clicking a lane isolates spans from that logical thread and updates the URL deep-link.
Rollout badges appear on spans where rollout metadata is present; clicking badge navigates to the rollout detail panel in Console.
Scrubber playback accurately steps through spans and preserves highlighted lane state; playback position is reflected in the shareable URL.
Filters for correlation-id and rollout variant return client-visible results and support copyable query strings.
Performance: rendering a representative 500-span trace in compact mode should complete under 250ms on a modern laptop in Chrome (PX test).
implementation_notes: Engineering spike requested: ENG to evaluate server-side lane annotation prototype (ENG-41990).
Telemetry: add events for lane-toggle, playback-start, and rollout-badge-click for feature telemetry.
Backend: add optional 'lane_id' and 'lane_edges' fields to trace proto with a feature flag for Dedicated/Private customers.
Design: deliver redlines, asset exports, and keyboard interaction spec after final review.
